historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (16.4% 5yr, 14.1% 3yr) is less than half the revenue CAGR (36.6% / 27.7%); equity growth is paid-in capital from SBC and the Wolt share issue rather than retained earnings (accumulated deficit is still 4.5bn), so it is a weak growth anchor. Year-1 growth is set from the organic run-rate instead and happens to land at 16%.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs are undefined: EPS was negative until FY2024 (-3.68 FY2022, -1.42 FY2023, 0.29 FY2024, 2.13 FY2025). Owner-FCF series (company FCF less expensed and capitalised SBC less interest income): FY2023 1,349 - 1,249 - 152 = -52; FY2024 1,802 - 1,264 - 199 = 339; FY2025 1,826 - 1,244 - 211 = 371; TTM Q3-2026 682. CAGRs are undefined from a negative start. Reported FCF rose 35% over FY2023-FY2025 while owner FCF went from nil to 371: SBC plus interest absorbed about 80% of reported FCF in FY2025 and still absorbs 69% on a TTM basis.

scenario_narratives.base: US restaurant delivery keeps compounding on order frequency and DashPass penetration while grocery, retail and the Wolt and Deliveroo markets add a second leg; advertising lifts the net revenue margin slightly and offsets lower consumer fees. Organic revenue growth fades from 16% to 4% over ten years, taking revenue from 17bn to about 41bn. Cash EBITDA reaches 29% of revenue, about 4% of Marketplace GOV, a level that needs continued Dasher-cost efficiency and ad mix but no heroics. SBC, counted with the part capitalised into software, declines from 8% to 4.5% of revenue. The tax shield from the 3.1bn federal NOL is gone by year 5.
scenario_narratives.bull: Grocery and retail reach restaurant-like unit economics, advertising scales toward 2% of GOV, and international (Wolt, Deliveroo) converges on US margins. Growth holds in the high teens for three years and cash EBITDA reaches 34% of revenue, roughly 4.6% of GOV, with SBC down to 4% of revenue. This case needs three independent things to go right at once: new-vertical economics, ad monetisation and international density.
scenario_narratives.bear: Uber Eats and Amazon compress US share gains and take rate; city and state pay-floor and worker-classification rules (the New York and Seattle pattern, and the EU platform-work directive in the Wolt and Deliveroo markets) raise Dasher cost faster than fees can absorb; grocery stays a low-margin frequency product. Growth drops to 12% and fades to 3%, cash EBITDA stalls at 23% of revenue, where Q3-2026 already is before the excluded legal and regulatory costs, and SBC stays above 5.5% of revenue. A debt-funded Instacart integration that disappoints is the path most likely to produce this outcome. The terminal multiple is capped at 15x for a slower business.

valuation_philosophy.summary: DoorDash is valued on what is left for owners after paying employees in stock. Company FCF of 2.2bn (TTM) shrinks to 0.68bn once expensed SBC (1.12bn), SBC capitalised into software (0.25bn) and interest on the cash pile (0.15bn) are removed. The value therefore rests on margin expansion and SBC falling as a share of revenue over a ten-year build, not on current cash flow, and most of it sits in the terminal value. The recent profitability inflection is not extrapolated: year 1 is anchored to the Q3-2026 run-rate, cash tax ramps to a full 23%, and the discount rate is 10% in every scenario.
key_risks_to_valuation: Pending ~17bn Instacart acquisition (close end-2027 or H1-2028): not modelled; turns net cash into net debt and adds ~5% to the share count
Mature margin: each 1pp of terminal cash EBITDA margin is worth roughly 4-5% of base value; the 29% base assumption has never been achieved
SBC glide from 8% to 4.5% of revenue is an assumption, not a management commitment; 2.5bn of unrecognised RSU expense is already outstanding
Dasher pay-floor and classification regulation in the US, UK and EU
Adjusted EBITDA excludes legal and regulatory settlements that recur every year; the model deducts 1.5pp of revenue for them
Terminal value is the majority of enterprise value in every scenario

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 143.30-239.00
data_sources.financials: DASH 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet, cash flow, diluted shares, convertible notes, subsequent-events note), 10-K FY2025 (FCF reconciliation, SBC, NOLs), 10-Q Q3-2025 comparatives; DASH_Metrics.csv and kpis table for history and Marketplace GOV
data_sources.qualitative: 10-Q and 10-K MD&A and risk factors; DASH_Analysis.json not yet available at build time

inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 10-Q weighted-average diluted shares (440.314M; basic outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 is 411.954M Class A + 24.006M Class B = 435.96M). Held FLAT because SBC, including the portion capitalised into software, is fully expensed in the flows. Excluded as out-of-the-money or contingent: 9.4M shares under the 0% 2030 convertible notes (conversion price ~US$292, hedged up to the warrant strike), 9.4M warrants, and 9.34M CEO performance RSUs that vest only on stock-price goals. Stock consideration for the pending Instacart deal is NOT included (see notes).
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 + 9M-2026 - 9M-2025. Expensed SBC 1,051 + 848 - 775 = 1,124 (10-K FY2025 line 2548; 10-Q Q3-2026 line 2501). PLUS SBC capitalised into software and website development, 193 + 196 - 140 = 249 (non-cash supplemental line of the cash flow statement; 10-K line 3175, 10-Q line 1740): it is neither in the expense line nor in cash capex, so it escapes both reported FCF and adjusted EBITDA unless added here. No net-share-settlement tax outflow in financing since FY2021; employer payroll tax on awards is already inside operating cash flow.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. 10.0% in every scenario: US 10-year ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.2 (forward-looking, below the ~1.7 observed while loss-making) = ~10.3% cost of equity; debt is a 0% convertible, so capital is effectively all equity. Deliberately not below 10% for a company whose first GAAP profit was FY2024. Risk is charged once: no per-scenario WACC differences, the scenarios and their weights carry the dispersion.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent sits inside operating costs and operating cash flow, so the lease cost is already in the EBITDA margin. Lease liabilities (570) are therefore NOT in net debt, and lease_cost_pct_path is zero.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable non-controlling interests of 10 and a 3 loss attributable over nine months: immaterial, no adjustment.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (US consumer marketplace; routing table row 1). Fresh build, no prior DCF and no memory entry. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30 Sep 2026 rather than FY2025 because the balance-sheet anchor is 30 Sep 2026: compounding from FY2025 would count nine months of 2026 cash both in net cash and in year 1. TTM revenue 17,061 = 13,717 + 13,106 - 9,762; it already holds four full quarters of Deliveroo (closed 2 Oct 2025), so forward growth rates are organic. Reported FCF is the COMPANY definition (operating cash flow less PP&E less capitalised software): 1,826 + 1,949 - 1,572 = 2,203. The Metrics CSV free_cash_flow column deducts PP&E only and overstates FCF by the capitalised software spend (FY2025: 2,174 vs 1,826). Net cash = cash 5,053 + short-term investments 929 + long-term investments 805 = 6,787, less the 2030 convertible notes at 2,750 principal (carried at 2,728). Excluded from cash: restricted cash 301 + 144 (insurance trusts) and 660 of funds held at payment processors (offset by merchant and Dasher payables). Interest income is stripped because net cash is ~6x the owner-FCF base. ebitda_margin_path is a CASH margin: company adjusted EBITDA less ~1.5pp of revenue for the items the company excludes but pays every year (legal, tax and regulatory settlements 159, transaction costs 46 and restructuring 51 in 9M-2026). TTM adjusted EBITDA was 3,508 (20.6% of revenue); Q3-2026 alone was 1,060 (23.0%). Buybacks: 1,049 repurchased in H1-2026 (6.8M shares at 155.25), none in Q3; the flat count is partly funded, not fully. PENDING DEAL, NOT MODELLED: on 28 Oct 2026 DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart (Maplebear) for 65.00 per share, ~17bn equity value, up to 25% in stock at 0.3372 DASH shares per Instacart share (roughly 22M new shares at most), the rest in cash backed by a 13bn bridge; close expected end-2027 or H1-2028, subject to HSR and other approvals. This is a standalone valuation. On completion net cash of ~4bn becomes net debt of roughly 8-9bn and the count rises ~5%; the model must then be rebuilt with Instacart's flows. The deal risk is reflected only in the bear weight. No guidance paragraph was found in the 10-Q text; year 1 is anchored to the Q3-2026 run-rate. Analysis JSON was not available at build time.
warnings: Pending ~17bn Instacart acquisition is not in the flows, the net debt or the share count; this is a standalone value.
Metrics CSV free_cash_flow excludes capitalised software and overstates company-defined FCF (FY2025 2,174 vs 1,826); the DCF uses the company definition.

base.narrative: Organic growth fades from 16% to 4%; cash EBITDA margin climbs from 21% to 29% of revenue (about 4% of Marketplace GOV at a 13.5% take rate, against 3.1% in Q3-2026); SBC including the capitalised portion falls from 8.05% to 4.5% of revenue; cash tax ramps from ~4% today to 23% as the 3.1bn federal NOL is consumed.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% rather than the 15% default: the standalone balance sheet carries no refinancing risk, but the signed Instacart deal swaps ~4bn of net cash for ~8-9bn of net debt and adds antitrust and integration risk that the flows do not show, on top of live pay-floor regulation. Base 50%: margin expansion to ~4% of GOV extends a five-year trend. Bull 30% rather than 35%: it needs grocery economics, advertising and international density to all deliver.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
